title: Coral and the Choir
premise: Ines Yarrow keeps the ledgers of the Choir, a guild that trades in impossible things through a gate that should have stayed shut since the country behind it drowned. When the old gods of that drowned land begin answering prayers on this side of the water, every debt in Ines's ledgers comes due at once — including his own inheritance: he is the last blood-heir of the gate's original builders. Hunted by the Choir's enforcers and guided by Coral, a smuggler-priestess who loves him against her vows, Ines must find the door out of a country that no longer exists before the gods' return drowns this one too. He ends it by paying the gate with his name instead of his life, erasing himself from every ledger to seal the way shut — remembered only by Coral, who carries what the ledgers cannot.
about_author: N. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records from port cities that no longer appear on maps. They write fantasy about paperwork, faith, and the people who keep both honest.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ines Yarrow audits the Choir's ledgers beneath a gate sealed for two hundred years, discovering entries that update themselves — debts being paid by someone unseen. His POV establishes his careful, lonely competence. The emotional beat is unease: the numbers are right, which frightens him more than wrong ones would.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in Salt
chapters.summary: In Coral's POV, a fisherman's prayer to a drowned god is answered with a tide of saltwater inland, and she smuggles the man past the Choir's checkpoints. She recognizes Ines's name among those the god whispered. The beat is dread mixed with longing — she has loved Ines from across the ledger desk for years.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes Me
chapters.summary: Ines finds his own birth recorded in a ledger older than the Choir itself, naming him heir of the gate-builders. The Choir's Provost summons him; Coral warns him not to go. He goes anyway. The emotional beat is vertigo — the ordered life he built was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: The Provost's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: The Provost reveals the Choir has been feeding the gate small sacrifices for centuries to keep it dormant, and now wants Ines as the final payment. Coral breaks her vows to break him out. Told in alternating close thirds. The beat is betrayal curdling into resolve: justice won't come from the law that owns them both.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Fugitives now, they follow roads that rearrange themselves toward the drowned country, guided by Coral's forbidden liturgy. A village worshipping a returned god shows them what answered prayers cost. The beat is tenderness under pressure — love admitted aloud because tomorrow is no longer guaranteed.

chapters.title: The Drowned Country's Shore
chapters.summary: They reach the coast where the old nation sank and find it risen partway, its capital half-restored, full of the dead who think they never died. Ines's blood opens doors here without his consent. The beat is grief — walking through his inheritance like a ghost haunting his own family home.

chapters.title: Audience with the Tide
chapters.summary: The old gods offer Ines restoration: his ancestors' kingdom reborn, his name made great, if he opens the gate fully. Coral argues duty to the living over loyalty to the dead. The beat is temptation sharpened into clarity — he sees that inheritance can be a leash dressed as a crown.

chapters.title: Every Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: The Choir's enforcers storm the risen city to take the gate by force while the gods' return floods the borderlands. Coral holds the liturgy line alone; Ines chooses neither side. The climax begins. The beat is fury and sacrifice — justice outside the law means accepting no one will thank you.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: At the gate's heart, Ines writes himself out of existence — surrendering his name, his records, his memory in every ledger — as the final payment that seals it. Coral sings him through the closing. The emotional beat is devastating peace: he saves everyone by agreeing to be forgotten.

chapters.title: Kept, Not Written
chapters.summary: Coral returns to a world that has no record of Ines Yarrow, where the ledgers are blank where he should be. She begins an unwritten ledger of her own, keeping him alive in memory and story. The beat is bittersweet hope — some inheritances are chosen, and love outlasts the paper it's written on.
